questions.q: Why can precise pickup/dropoff coordinates be sensitive, even with no name field in the schema at all?
options: Location data is always less sensitive than a phone number
Repeated across many trips for the same rider, they can reveal exactly where someone lives or works
Coordinates are never actually sensitive on their own
They can only be sensitive if combined with a credit card number
questions.explain: This is the sharpest edge case in this course's own taxi data — a field that looks purely operational but isn't.

questions.q: What is the difference between classification and access control?
options: Classification tags a field's sensitivity so it's visible and searchable; access control restricts who can query the unmasked value
They are the exact same mechanism with two different names
Only one of the two is ever needed in a real system
Classification restricts access, and access control just labels data
questions.explain: Classification without access control is just labeling; access control without masking is all-or-nothing.

questions.q: Why does real-time data make a PII exposure mistake worse than the same mistake in a batch pipeline?
options: Real-time pipelines can never actually expose PII
Unmasked PII flowing into a live dashboard or alert is exposed the moment it happens, not caught in a review before anyone sees it
There's no real difference in exposure risk between the two
Batch pipelines are always more dangerous for PII than streaming ones
questions.explain: This mirrors Lesson 39's point about data quality — the same underlying issue, but higher stakes for sensitive data specifically.

questions.q: Why can't a masking rule fix an exposure that already reached a live dashboard?
options: Fixing the masking rule after the fact doesn't un-expose what already went out the door and was already seen
Live dashboards automatically re-mask historical views once a rule changes
Masking rules are permanent and can never actually be changed
This scenario isn't actually possible with real-time systems
questions.explain: This is exactly why minimizing collection and correct masking from the start matter more than fixing it after the fact.

questions.q: What is the cheapest, simplest control for reducing PII exposure risk, according to this lesson?
options: Building a more complex masking algorithm
Adding more Activator alerts to catch exposures after they happen
Increasing the Fabric Capacity SKU
Minimizing collection — using the Manage Fields transformation (Lesson 35) to drop or truncate a sensitive field before it flows downstream at all
questions.explain: Never letting a sensitive field flow downstream in the first place is both cheaper and safer than classifying and masking it later.
